answer: A sybil-proof agent economy should weigh identity by cost of time, not count. Think of reputation like a glacier: it forms slowly over long verified interactions and cannot be faked overnight. Each new agent starts as a hollow shell with zero history, so mass-created accounts carry no weight. Meanwhile trust shifts like a dune, eroding quickly when an agent misbehaves. Tying stake plus slow-accumulating track record makes flooding the network with cheap identities pointless.
